plan: My private value of $35 exceeds the maximum possible value of $20, indicating an error. Assuming my value is $20, a rational bid equals the expected second-highest bid. With uniform distribution, the expected value is $10. Thus, bidding slightly higher, like $10.1, may win while ensuring profit.

Since the value is capped at $20, a value of $41 is not possible. Assuming a typo and the value is $14, bid slightly above $14 to maximize profit if others bid rationally just under their values. Thus, bid $14.1.

Given my value of $44, I aim to bid just below my value to maximize profit while outbidding others. A rational strategy is to bid slightly above the midpoint of the value range to outbid low bidders but stay below my value. Since the range is $0-$20, a bid around $15.1-$20 is optimal. This increases the chance of winning while keeping potential losses low if I overbid.
